comment: REVIEWED CITATION SITES — the ONLY suppression mechanism for
checks/check_spec_citations.py. Read that gate's docstring before adding a row.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, and it has exactly ONE legitimate use. The gate reports a citation
whose section does not exist in the document the surrounding prose names. There is one
class of text for which that is the CORRECT thing to write: prose whose subject IS the
non-existent section. ARC 018's correction note in checks/check_order_path_bans.py says
'There is no §2.1 in that document' three lines after naming the document, and a gate that
reddens the record of a fix is reddening the fix (doctrine B.4).
IT IS NOT A PLACE TO PARK A BAD CITATION. A citation that is simply wrong is repaired by
correcting it, and ARC 019 repaired one that way rather than suppressing it:
checks/check_derived_claims.py cited '§2.4' of the check contract, which has no 2.4, and the
docstring now cites `debug.md` §7.4 (doctrine C.4) instead. The correction is recorded in
that file. Adding a row here for a citation you could have fixed is the widening the
suppression mechanism exists to prevent.
WHAT A SUPPRESSION IS. One reviewed SITE. The key is (file, section, document) — all three
must match or the suppression does not apply.
WHAT A SUPPRESSION IS NOT, and these are structural, not conventions:
* NOT file-level. `section` and `document` are required keys and an entry missing either
is REJECTED and reported as a violation. There is no `file`-only form.
* NOT directory-level. No path prefix or glob is honoured anywhere in the gate.
* NOT line-keyed. `debug.md` §8 failure mode #4 is the stale literal anchor and a line
number is one — which is the argument this gate itself makes about `§2A:71`. Reformat
the file and the suppression still holds; rewrite the sentence to cite a different
section and it stops holding, which is the correct behaviour.
SELF-EXPIRING. An entry matching NO citation in the current tree is a VIOLATION, not a
no-op. A review applies to text that exists; when the text is corrected, the review is
spent and the row must go. An entry with an empty `justification` or `reviewed_in` is also
a VIOLATION — an unsigned suppression is not a review.
VISIBLE ON EVERY RUN. Every applied suppression is printed in the gate's `evidence` as
`REVIEWED SUPPRESSION <site> — <justification>`. A suppression can go stale but it cannot
go invisible.
MEASURED, ARC 019, against the tree at 8cdfdcb: the governed scope produced TWO
non-resolutions. One was a real defect and was fixed (check_derived_claims.py, above); one
is the row below. One review owed across three governed roots. Re-derive rather than
trusting this line — it is history, and history is append-only:
.venv/bin/python checks/check_spec_citations.py

reviewed.justification: THE TEXT'S SUBJECT IS THE PHANTOM ITSELF. This is ARC 018's CITATION CORRECTION block, whose whole content is the finding that the frozen spec has no §2.1 — it names the document and then says, in the next sentence, that the section does not exist in it. Deleting the citation would delete the record of the correction, and the record is what stops the phantom being re-derived by a future arc reading the ban and wondering what authorises it. The three REAL anchors are stated in the same docstring and all three resolve under this gate: §2A:71, §4:241, §12A:830.
reviewed.re_review_if: the CITATION CORRECTION block is ever deleted or rewritten to stop quoting the phantom — at which point this row becomes a STALE SUPPRESSION and the gate will say so
